result.title: In-Context Learning Can Help Vision-Language Models Overcome Training Priors
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) learn strong statistical regularities during training, which can make them fail to properly respond to visual evidence when input images violate those regularities. It is challenging to disambiguate these prior-induced errors from errors caused by the model missing the underlying visual capabilities. In this work, we use controlled visual in-context learning to encourage the model to focus on the visual evidence, and demonstrate that this alone is frequently sufficient to correct the errors -- suggesting that the models in fact do possess the relevant visual capabilities. Specifically, we show that across five vision-centric tasks, demonstrations yield large gains on prior-conflicting counterfactual examples ($+27.2\%$ for Qwen3-VL 235B and $+15.1\%$ for Qwen3-VL 32B) while leaving accuracy on prior-aligned examples nearly unchanged. These findings generalize across five VLM families with gains from $+9.7\%$ to $+30.3\%$. We analyze visual representations and find that demonstrations indeed redirect attention toward grounding cues while reducing reliance on cues that support the learned prior. Finally, we find that in-context learning is limited when the underlying visual capability is weak or absent. Together, these results show that current VLMs possess visual grounding capabilities that standard evaluations may overlook, underscoring the need for controlled evaluation design in diagnosing and improving model capability.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用受控的视觉 in-context learning（提供示例演示）研究 VLM 在图像违反训练先验时能否依据视觉证据作答，发现演示可大幅纠正先验导致的错误（五个任务上 Qwen3-VL 235B +27.2%、32B +15.1%，跨五个 VLM 家族 +9.7%~+30.3%），且表示分析显示注意被重新导向 grounding 线索；当底层视觉能力弱或缺失时提升有限。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作直接诊断 VLM 是否真正使用视觉证据、并区分训练先验驱动的错误与视觉能力缺失，与「视觉旁路/信息坍缩」及答案是否依赖视觉内容的议题高度相关；其注意重定向分析与受控评测设计可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据的使用与评价方式。
